quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Late' in the sentence.
quests.definition: Arriving after the expected time.
quests.contextSentence: Heavy rain left morning commuter trains slightly ___.
quests.usageExample: Heavy rain left morning commuter trains slightly delayed.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Late' describes people or trains off schedule. 'Delayed' means held back by a specific cause or announcement.
quests.explanation: Natural — transport schedules held up by causes use 'delayed'.
quests.hint: 'Late' describes people or trains off schedule — think of the 'Flight Board' sense starting with 'D'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Early' in the sentence.
quests.definition: Happening on time or ahead of expectation.
quests.contextSentence: Sending a ___ reply helps guests book with confidence.
quests.usageExample: Sending a prompt reply helps guests book with confidence.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Early' means before the clock time. 'Prompt' praises fast, reliable response right on time.
quests.explanation: Natural — 'prompt' praises fast, punctual service.
quests.hint: 'Early' means before the clock time — think of the 'Service Desk' sense starting with 'P'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'End' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To bring an activity or task to completion.
quests.contextSentence: Workers hope to ___ painting the fence before dark.
quests.usageExample: Workers hope to finish painting the fence before dark.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'End' applies to stories, meetings, or streets. 'Finish' means completing work you were actively doing.
quests.explanation: Natural — completing personal tasks takes 'finish'.
quests.hint: 'End' applies to stories, meetings, or streets — think of the 'Homework Task' sense starting with 'F'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Right' in the sentence.
quests.definition: Free from mistakes or accurate.
quests.contextSentence: Double-check every number so the invoice is ___.
quests.usageExample: Double-check every number so the invoice is correct.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Right' works for sides (`right hand`), justice, and answers. 'Correct' highlights accuracy against rules or facts.
quests.explanation: Natural — factual or test accuracy fits 'correct'.
quests.hint: 'Right' works for sides (`right hand`), justice, and answers — think of the 'Quiz Check' sense starting with 'C'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Wrong' in the sentence.
quests.definition: Not matching facts or truth.
quests.contextSentence: The alarm triggered after one ___ reading from the sensor.
quests.usageExample: The alarm triggered after a false reading from the sensor.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Wrong' covers bad choices, errors, and wrong turns. 'False' describes invented claims or fake items.
quests.explanation: Natural — untrue claims and statements are 'false'.
quests.hint: 'Wrong' covers bad choices, errors, and wrong turns — think of the 'News Check' sense starting with 'F'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Full' in the sentence.
quests.definition: Holding as much as possible inside.
quests.contextSentence: Shoppers avoided the ___ mall on holiday weekends.
quests.usageExample: Shoppers avoided the crowded mall on holiday weekends.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Full' describes containers (`full cup`) or schedules. 'Crowded' specifically means packed with too many people.
quests.explanation: Natural — spaces packed with people are 'crowded'.
quests.hint: 'Full' describes containers (`full cup`) or schedules — think of the 'Subway Rush' sense starting with 'C'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Save' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To protect from harm or loss.
quests.contextSentence: Coast guards worked fast to ___ the stranded sailors.
quests.usageExample: Coast guards worked fast to rescue the stranded sailors.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Save' covers money (`save cash`), files, and lives. 'Rescue' means physically pulling someone out of danger.
quests.explanation: Natural — freeing someone from danger uses 'rescue'.
quests.hint: 'Save' covers money (`save cash`), files, and lives — think of the 'Mountain Team' sense starting with 'R'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Spend' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To use money, time, or supplies.
quests.contextSentence: Leaving the tap running will ___ gallons of clean water.
quests.usageExample: Leaving the tap running will waste gallons of clean water.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Spend' is neutral usage (`spend time reading`). 'Waste' judges that the time or resource gave zero benefit.
quests.explanation: Natural — throwing away good resources is 'waste'.
quests.hint: 'Spend' is neutral usage (`spend time reading`) — think of the 'Leftover Food' sense starting with 'W'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Pay' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To transfer or gain money for work.
quests.contextSentence: Interns ___ valuable coding experience on real apps.
quests.usageExample: Interns earn valuable coding experience on real apps.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Pay' means handing out cash (`pay bills`). 'Earn' means working to deserve your wages or trust.
quests.explanation: Natural — money received by working takes 'earn'.
quests.hint: 'Pay' means handing out cash (`pay bills`) — think of the 'Summer Job' sense starting with 'E'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Break' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To separate or damage a surface.
quests.contextSentence: Dropping the mug on stone made the handle ___.
quests.usageExample: Dropping the mug on stone made the handle crack.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Break' splits things into pieces or breaks rules. 'Crack' creates a thin split line without falling apart.
quests.explanation: Natural — thin split lines on glass or screens take 'crack'.
quests.hint: 'Break' splits things into pieces or breaks rules — think of the 'Cold Glass' sense starting with 'C'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Shut' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To move a door or opening so nothing passes through.
quests.contextSentence: Remember to ___ the bedroom window before it rains.
quests.usageExample: Remember to close the bedroom window before it rains.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Shut' fits firmly closing doors and lids (`shut the gate`). 'Close' is calmer and works for banks, shops, eyes, and accounts.
quests.explanation: Natural — business hours and accounts always use 'close'.
quests.hint: 'Shut' fits firmly closing doors and lids (`shut the gate`) — think of the 'Store Hours' sense starting with 'C'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Build' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To make something by joining parts or ideas.
quests.contextSentence: Musicians ___ new melodies using simple piano chords.
quests.usageExample: Musicians create new melodies using simple piano chords.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Build' joins physical bricks or code. 'Create' emphasizes original imagination like art, music, or jobs.
quests.explanation: Natural — original artwork and designs use 'create'.
quests.hint: 'Build' joins physical bricks or code — think of the 'Art Poster' sense starting with 'C'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Sweet' in the sentence.
quests.definition: Having a taste like sugar or honey.
quests.contextSentence: Skip ___ snacks and pack fresh apples instead.
quests.usageExample: Skip sugary snacks and pack fresh apples instead.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Sweet' fits fruit, kindness, and desserts. 'Sugary' specifically warns of heavy added sugar.
quests.explanation: Natural — nutrition warnings about added sugar use 'sugary'.
quests.hint: 'Sweet' fits fruit, kindness, and desserts — think of the 'Health Label' sense starting with 'S'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Dry' in the sentence.
quests.definition: Having little or no moisture.
quests.contextSentence: Cactus plants thrive across the ___ southern plains.
quests.usageExample: Cactus plants thrive across the arid southern plains.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Dry' fits towels, skin, and humor. 'Arid' describes desert land that receives almost no rain.
quests.explanation: Natural — dry climates and deserts use 'arid'.
quests.hint: 'Dry' fits towels, skin, and humor — think of the 'Desert Map' sense starting with 'A'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Dark' in the sentence.
quests.definition: Having little or low light.
quests.contextSentence: Before the movie starts, the theater lights turn ___.
quests.usageExample: Before the movie starts, the theater lights turn dim.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Dark' covers night skies and deep colors. 'Dim' means faint lighting where shapes remain slightly visible.
quests.explanation: Natural — weak lamps and low brightness take 'dim'.
quests.hint: 'Dark' covers night skies and deep colors — think of the 'Reading Lamp' sense starting with 'D'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Strong' in the sentence.
quests.definition: Having high physical force or strong influence.
quests.contextSentence: Doctors used a ___ microscope to study tiny cells.
quests.usageExample: Doctors used a powerful microscope to study tiny cells.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Strong' fits muscles, coffee, and wind. 'Powerful' highlights huge motors, computers, or major authority.
quests.explanation: Natural — engines, nations, and speech impact use 'powerful'.
quests.hint: 'Strong' fits muscles, coffee, and wind — think of the 'Rocket Engine' sense starting with 'P'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Weak' in the sentence.
quests.definition: Lacking strength or easily damaged.
quests.contextSentence: Handle the ___ antique teacup with two hands.
quests.usageExample: Handle the fragile antique teacup with two hands.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Weak' fits muscles, tea, or arguments. 'Fragile' warns that delicate glass or eggs can shatter easily.
quests.explanation: Natural — breakable items require 'fragile'.
quests.hint: 'Weak' fits muscles, tea, or arguments — think of the 'Parcel Box' sense starting with 'F'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Sleepy' in the sentence.
quests.definition: Ready to fall asleep.
quests.contextSentence: Pull over safely if you begin to feel ___ on the highway.
quests.usageExample: Pull over safely if you begin to feel drowsy on the highway.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Sleepy' works for cozy bedtime moods or quiet towns. 'Drowsy' specifically warns of heavy eyelids, often from medicine.
quests.explanation: Natural — pill side effects always warn of feeling 'drowsy'.
quests.hint: 'Sleepy' works for cozy bedtime moods or quiet towns — think of the 'Medicine Label' sense starting with 'D'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Pull' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To move something toward you or along a surface.
quests.contextSentence: Children helped ___ the wet sled up the snowy hill.
quests.usageExample: Children helped drag the wet sled up the snowy hill.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Pull' covers doors, ropes, and muscles. 'Drag' emphasizes heavy friction scraping across the ground.
quests.explanation: Natural — scraping something heavy along the floor is 'drag'.
quests.hint: 'Pull' covers doors, ropes, and muscles — think of the 'Heavy Bag' sense starting with 'D'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Throw' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To send an object through the air.
quests.contextSentence: She decided to ___ a coin into the wishing fountain.
quests.usageExample: She decided to toss a coin into the wishing fountain.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Throw' can be fast or forceful (`throw a fastball`). 'Toss' means a light, casual short-distance flip.
quests.explanation: Natural — short casual passes take 'toss'.
quests.hint: 'Throw' can be fast or forceful (`throw a fastball`) — think of the 'Salad Bowl' sense starting with 'T'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Hold' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To support an object with your hands or body.
quests.contextSentence: Backpack straps make it easier to ___ heavy textbooks.
quests.usageExample: Backpack straps make it easier to carry heavy textbooks.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Hold' keeps something still in place. 'Carry' moves something from one place to another.
quests.explanation: Natural — transporting items while moving uses 'carry'.
quests.hint: 'Hold' keeps something still in place — think of the 'Airport Bag' sense starting with 'C'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Join' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To bring two or more things together.
quests.contextSentence: Steel bridges ___ both sides of the wide river.
quests.usageExample: Steel bridges connect both sides of the wide river.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Join' adds you to a club or glues pieces. 'Connect' links cables, flights, devices, or ideas.
quests.explanation: Natural — cables, routers, and transit routes 'connect'.
quests.hint: 'Join' adds you to a club or glues pieces — think of the 'Wi-Fi Setup' sense starting with 'C'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Same' in the sentence.
quests.definition: Sharing identical or nearly matching features.
quests.contextSentence: Even though their styles differ, the siblings think ___.
quests.usageExample: Even though their styles differ, the siblings think alike.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Same' goes before a noun (`the same coat`). 'Alike' goes after the verb (`look alike`) without a noun.
quests.explanation: Natural — 'alike' works after 'look/are' comparing two things.
quests.hint: Fits expressions like "look ___" — starts with 'A'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Different' in the sentence.
quests.definition: Not matching others.
quests.contextSentence: This island hosts one ___ bird species found nowhere else.
quests.usageExample: This island hosts a unique bird species found nowhere else.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Different' simply means not identical. 'Unique' celebrates being one-of-a-kind with no second copy.
quests.explanation: Natural — one-of-a-kind craft designs earn 'unique'.
quests.hint: 'Different' simply means not identical — think of the 'Handcrafted Mug' sense starting with 'U'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Trip' in the sentence.
quests.definition: A visit from one place to another.
quests.contextSentence: Visitors booked a bus ___ around the historic castle.
quests.usageExample: Visitors booked a bus tour around the historic castle.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Trip' covers any travel stay. 'Tour' means visiting multiple stops with a planned route or guide.
quests.explanation: Natural — guided walks with multiple sights are a 'tour'.
quests.hint: 'Trip' covers any travel stay — think of the 'Museum Visit' sense starting with 'T'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Park' in the sentence.
quests.definition: An outdoor space with plants and paths.
quests.contextSentence: Bees buzzed around roses in the quiet palace ___.
quests.usageExample: Bees buzzed around roses in the quiet palace garden.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Park' is public space for walking, sports, or picnics. 'Garden' focuses on tended flowers or home vegetables.
quests.explanation: Natural — cultivated home vegetables grow in a 'garden'.
quests.hint: 'Park' is public space for walking, sports, or picnics — think of the 'Backyard Plot' sense starting with 'G'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Climb' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To travel upward or over rough trails.
quests.contextSentence: Pack sturdy boots before you ___ the rocky canyon trail.
quests.usageExample: Pack sturdy boots before you hike the rocky canyon trail.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Climb' goes vertically up ladders, stairs, or rocks. 'Hike' means walking long scenic nature trails.
quests.explanation: Natural — long trail walks in nature use 'hike'.
quests.hint: 'Climb' goes vertically up ladders, stairs, or rocks — think of the 'Trail Map' sense starting with 'H'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Learn' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To gain skill or knowledge.
quests.contextSentence: Students meet in groups to ___ before Friday quizzes.
quests.usageExample: Students meet in groups to study before Friday quizzes.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Learn' marks successfully gaining knowledge. 'Study' means spending focused time reading or practicing.
quests.explanation: Natural — putting in reading hours takes 'study'.
quests.hint: 'Learn' marks successfully gaining knowledge — think of the 'Library Quiet' sense starting with 'S'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Clear' in the sentence.
quests.definition: Easy to see or understand.
quests.contextSentence: The menu offers ___ rice or spicy fried noodles.
quests.usageExample: The menu offers plain rice or spicy fried noodles.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Clear' means easy to hear, see through, or grasp. 'Plain' means simple, unflavored, or unmistakably obvious.
quests.explanation: Natural — simple unflavored food is 'plain'.
quests.hint: 'Clear' means easy to hear, see through, or grasp — think of the 'Yogurt Cup' sense starting with 'P'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Smart' in the sentence.
quests.definition: Showing good judgment or quick thinking.
quests.contextSentence: Taking time to listen before deciding is always ___.
quests.usageExample: Taking time to listen before deciding is always wise.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Smart' praises quick answers, tech, or sharp style. 'Wise' honors deep life experience and calm judgment.
quests.explanation: Natural — thoughtful long-term judgment is 'wise'.
quests.hint: 'Smart' praises quick answers, tech, or sharp style — think of the 'Grandma Advice' sense starting with 'W'.
